must_not_miss.text: The signature block: CHIEF JUSTICE G.B. MORAWETZ.
must_not_miss.why: Page 4 is a 252-character orphan page. Easy to skip entirely.

must_not_miss.text: The Incremental PBGF Assessment Payment — a second stayed payment, amount not stated.
must_not_miss.why: Sits behind the $842,018.34 in the same sentence. Extractions reliably capture the number and drop the unquantified second payment.

must_not_miss.text: The FSRA carve-out: the stay does not preclude FSRA from asserting a claim.
must_not_miss.why: Reverses the paragraph it sits in. Dropping it inverts the meaning of the order.

must_not_miss.text: The 30-day deemed-withdrawal rule: an Interim CV Applicant who does not re-elect in writing loses the commuted value transfer and keeps only a deferred pension.
must_not_miss.why: The consequence clause runs across a page break — precisely where section-chunked extraction loses text.

must_not_miss.text: Derek Harland appears in two capacities: deponent of the Affidavit of Service (p. 2) and counsel at TGF (p. 5).
must_not_miss.why: Requires joining the front and back of the document. A per-section extractor sees the two mentions in different chunks and will usually emit two unlinked entities, or one.

must_not_miss.why: Buried in a long procedural sentence about service. These are the human beings the 65.8% ratio is being applied to; an extractor tuned to institutions will drop them.

X.summary: This Ontario Superior Court Commercial List order in Laurentian University of Sudbury’s CCAA proceeding resolves pension-related interim commuted value transfers and a pension fund assessment issue. The court permits Laurentian, as sponsor and administrator of its pension plan, to use a 65.8% transfer ratio from the most recent actuarial valuation for eligible interim commuted value transfers, and requires affected applicants to make a re-election within 30 days of notice. It also stays a $842,018.34 Pension Benefits Guarantee Fund assessment payment due March 30, 2021, together with any incremental amount linked to a later actuarial valuation, while preserving the Financial Services Regulatory Authority of Ontario’s ability to assert a claim.

key_facts.fact: The Ontario Superior Court of Justice Commercial List issued an order in Court File No. CV-21-00656040-00CL in Laurentian University of Sudbury’s CCAA proceeding.
The order was made by Chief Justice G.B. Morawetz on March 17, 2021.
Laurentian University of Sudbury acted as the applicant in the CCAA proceeding and brought the motion for pension-related relief.
Laurentian, as sponsor and administrator of the Pension Plan, was permitted to transfer commuted values using a transfer ratio of 65.8%.
key_facts.quote: transfer ratio equal to 65.8% (the ' Transfer Ratio ')

key_facts.fact: The 65.8% transfer ratio came from the most recently filed actuarial valuation report for the Pension Plan, effective January 1, 2020, and filed with the Financial Services Regulatory Authority of Ontario in December 2020.

Interim CV Applicants who had elected a commuted value transfer were to receive a re-election form and had 30 days from notice of the order to choose an immediate or deferred pension, or a commuted value transfer based on the transfer ratio.

An Interim CV Applicant who did not make a written election within 30 days of notice would be deemed to have withdrawn the commuted value transfer application and would retain entitlement to a deferred pension.
The order states that future adjustments to the transfer ratio must be established under the Pension Benefits Act and its regulations, or by further court order.

A Pension Benefits Guarantee Fund assessment payment of $842,018.34 due on March 30, 2021 was stayed and suspended under paragraph 12 of the Amended and Restated Initial Order dated February 11, 2021.
key_facts.quote: the payment due on March 30, 2021 in the amount of $842,018.34

key_facts.fact: The stay also covered any incremental amount owing in respect of Laurentian’s pro rata portion of assessment fees for the Pension Plan for the pre-filing period July 1, 2018 to June 30, 2019, arising from the December 2020 filing of a new actuarial valuation report.
The order provides that neither Laurentian nor its directors, officers, employees, agents, advisors, or consultants incur liability because of the stay and suspension of the PBGF assessment payments.
The court left open the Financial Services Regulatory Authority’s ability to assert a claim against Laurentian for the PBGF assessment payment or the incremental PBGF assessment payment.

The order requests recognition and assistance from courts, tribunals, and regulatory or administrative bodies in Canada and the United States to give effect to the order and to assist the Monitor and Laurentian.

Y.summary: This is a court order made by Chief Justice Morawetz of the Ontario Superior Court of Justice (Commercial List) on March 17, 2021, in the CCAA restructuring proceeding of Laurentian University of Sudbury. The order addresses two pension-related matters: it authorizes LU to apply a Transfer Ratio of 65.8% to commuted value transfers for certain pension plan members ("Interim CV Applicants") who had elected 100% commuted value transfers, and it confirms that LU's Pension Benefits Guarantee Fund assessment payment of $842,018.34 (due March 30, 2021) and a related incremental payment are stayed under the Amended and Restated Initial Order dated February 11, 2021. Interim CV Applicants are given 30 days to re-elect either an immediate/deferred pension or a commuted value transfer at the 65.8% ratio; failure to elect within that period deems them to have withdrawn their commuted value application.

key_facts.fact: The CCAA proceeding for Laurentian University of Sudbury was assigned court file number CV-21-00656040-00CL in the Ontario Superior Court of Justice (Commercial List).
The Amended and Restated Initial Order in the LU CCAA proceeding was dated February 11, 2021.
key_facts.quote: paragraph 12 of the Amended and Restated Initial Order of this Court dated February 11, 2021

key_facts.fact: The court authorized LU to apply a Transfer Ratio of 65.8% to commuted value transfers from the Pension Plan for Interim CV Applicants, based on the most recently filed actuarial valuation report effective January 1, 2020, filed with the Financial Services Regulatory Authority of Ontario in December 2020.
The actuarial valuation report for the LU Pension Plan was effective January 1, 2020 and was filed with FSRAO in December 2020.

Interim CV Applicants who had elected 100% commuted value transfers must re-elect within 30 days of notice of the order to either receive an immediate or deferred pension or a commuted value transfer at the 65.8% Transfer Ratio; failure to re-elect within 30 days deems them to have withdrawn their commuted value application and they retain entitlement to a deferred pension.
LU's pro rata PBGF assessment payment of $842,018.34, due March 30, 2021, relating to the Pension Plan for the pre-filing period July 1, 2019 to June 30, 2020, was stayed and suspended.
key_facts.quote: the payment due on March 30, 2021 in the amount of $842,018.34 in respect of LU's pro rata portion of assessment fees payable to the Pension Benefits Guarantee Fund relating to the Pension Plan for the pre-filing period of July 1, 2019 to June 30, 2020

key_facts.fact: An incremental PBGF assessment payment relating to the pre-filing period July 1, 2018 to June 30, 2019, triggered by the December 2020 filing of a new actuarial valuation report, was also stayed.
The stay of PBGF payments does not preclude the Financial Services Regulatory Authority from asserting a claim against LU in respect of those payments.
The order was signed by Chief Justice G.B. Morawetz.

LU's counsel in the CCAA proceeding is Thornton Grout Finnigan LLP, with lawyers D.J. Miller (LSO# 344393P), Mitchell W. Grossell (LSO# 69993I), Andrew Hanrahan (LSO# 78003K), and Derek Harland (LSO# 79504N).
The motion was heard by videoconference via Zoom due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
Five Interim CV Applicants appeared at the hearing: Caleb Leduc, Brady Zapalski, Ann Pegoraro, William Oxley, and Sheila McGillis.

The Notice of Motion was dated March 8, 2021; the Brinkman affidavit was sworn March 8, 2021; the Second Report of the Monitor was dated March 11, 2021; the Affidavit of Service of Derek Harland was sworn March 10, 2021.
The Initial Haché Affidavit was sworn by Dr. Robert Haché on January 30, 2021.
key_facts.quote: the affidavit of Dr. Robert Haché sworn January 30, 2021

Z.summary: This is a CCAA pension order issued by Chief Justice Morawetz of the Ontario Superior Court of Justice on March 17, 2021, in the restructuring proceeding of Laurentian University of Sudbury (Court File No. CV-21-00656040-00CL). The order addresses two pension-related matters: it authorizes LU to apply a reduced Transfer Ratio of 65.8% (drawn from an actuarial valuation effective January 1, 2020) to all pending commuted value transfer requests from Interim CV Applicants, and it stays two Pension Benefits Guarantee Fund assessment payments — a $842,018.34 payment due March 30, 2021 for the pre-filing period July 1, 2019 to June 30, 2020, plus an incremental amount for July 1, 2018 to June 30, 2019 — pursuant to the Amended and Restated Initial Order dated February 11, 2021. Interim CV Applicants who had elected a 100% commuted value transfer must re-elect within 30 days of notice, or be deemed to have withdrawn their commuted value application and reverted to a deferred pension.

key_facts.fact: The Ontario Superior Court of Justice (Commercial List) issued this pension order on March 17, 2021 in CCAA proceedings involving Laurentian University of Sudbury under Court File No. CV-21-00656040-00CL.
key_facts.quote: IN THE MATTER OF A PLAN OF COMPROMISE OR ARRANGEMENT OF LAURENTIAN UNIVERSITY OF SUDBURY

key_facts.fact: Chief Justice G.B. Morawetz presided over this motion, heard by videoconference via Zoom in Toronto, Ontario on March 17, 2021 due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
key_facts.quote: was heard this day by videoconference via Zoom in Toronto, Ontario due to the COVID-19 pandemic

key_facts.fact: LU is the sponsor and administrator of the Pension Plan that is the subject of this order.
The court authorized LU to apply a Transfer Ratio of 65.8% for commuted value transfers from the Pension Plan for all Interim CV Applicants.

The 65.8% Transfer Ratio was drawn from the most recently filed actuarial valuation report for the Pension Plan, effective January 1, 2020 and filed with the Financial Services Regulatory Authority of Ontario in December 2020.

Interim CV Applicants who had previously elected a 100% commuted value transfer must submit a re-election form in writing to LU within 30 days of notice of this order, choosing either an immediate or deferred pension or a reduced commuted value transfer at the 65.8% Transfer Ratio.
An Interim CV Applicant who does not re-elect within 30 days will be deemed to have withdrawn their commuted value application and will retain entitlement to a deferred pension.

The court stayed and suspended LU's PBGF Assessment Payment of $842,018.34, due on March 30, 2021, representing LU's pro rata share of Pension Benefits Guarantee Fund assessment fees for the pre-filing period July 1, 2019 to June 30, 2020, plus any interest and penalties.
key_facts.quote: payment due on March 30, 2021 in the amount of $842,018.34

key_facts.fact: The court also stayed the Incremental PBGF Assessment Payment owed by LU for the pre-filing period July 1, 2018 to June 30, 2019, which arose from the December 2020 filing of a new actuarial valuation report.
Both PBGF payment stays are pursuant to paragraph 12 of the Amended and Restated Initial Order of the court dated February 11, 2021.

The order expressly preserves the right of the Financial Services Regulatory Authority of Ontario to assert a claim against LU in respect of the stayed PBGF Assessment Payments, notwithstanding the stay.
LU's directors, officers, employees, agents, advisors, and consultants are protected from personal liability arising from the stay and suspension of the PBGF Assessment Payments.

The motion was supported by the Notice of Motion dated March 8, 2021, the affidavit of Dr. Robert Haché sworn January 30, 2021, the affidavit of Bobbie-Jo Brinkman sworn March 8, 2021, and the Second Report of the Monitor dated March 11, 2021.
Five named Interim CV Applicants appeared at the hearing: Caleb Leduc, Brady Zapalski, Ann Pegoraro, William Oxley, and Sheila McGillis.

Service was confirmed by the Affidavit of Service of Derek Harland sworn March 10, 2021; no one appeared for any other person on the service list or the remaining Interim CV Applicants despite due service.

Thornton Grout Finnigan LLP, based at 3200-100 Wellington Street West, TD West Tower, Toronto-Dominion Centre, Toronto ON M5K 1K7, acted as lawyers for LU as Applicant; counsel listed are D.J. Miller (LSO# 344393P), Mitchell W. Grossell (LSO# 69993I), Andrew Hanrahan (LSO# 78003K), and Derek Harland (LSO# 79504N).
